about.title: Atwater Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause harm in ways that often catch people off guard — a malfunctioning tool at a Shaffer Road warehouse job, a farm implement that fails during use near Winton Way, or a household appliance that sparks a fire. Atwater residents, many connected to Merced County's agricultural and logistics economy along SR-99, encounter industrial equipment, machinery, and consumer goods daily. When one of those products is defective, California law allows injured people to pursue compensation without proving the manufacturer was careless. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly — we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate whether a design flaw, manufacturing error, or missing warning label contributed to your injury. The attorney can also advise on preserving the product itself, since physical evidence is often central to these cases. There's no cost to you unless the attorney recovers compensation on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Atwater Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally doesn't require proof the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused harm. This can streamline what you need to show in a claim.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California product liability law. An attorney can help identify every party connected to the defective product.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Because the product itself is often the central piece of evidence, an attorney can advise you right away on how to store it safely and avoid losing your claim's strongest support.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless to file a claim?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that anyone acted negligently. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to confirm how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, and any broken pieces. Store it somewhere safe and avoid repairs or alterations. This preserved evidence can be important if an attorney later reviews the defect.
